note: First-time guide. One entry per screen; each shows once, then can be replayed from the Tips button. A step with no 'anchor' is a modal in the middle of the screen. A step with an 'anchor' (a CSS selector) points at that part of the page and outlines it. Plain words only: say what Plainflow is making and doing, not what the buttons are called. 'canvas' shows after the picture draws; 'answer' shows after Check it.

door.title: What this does
door.body: You'll describe an idea that uses people's data, in one sentence, then answer a few plain questions. Plainflow turns that into a picture of where the data goes, and reads the answer off the picture: can you do it, does your organisation's policy allow it, do you need a DPIA (a written check of what could go wrong for people), and what to do next.
door.aside: Nothing you type is sent anywhere; it stays in this browser until you save it. Use roles and groups, never people's names.

door.title: Start here
door.body: Say what you're checking: a new idea, something already running, a sensitivity level you already know, or an app you've built. Pick one and a sentence to fill in appears below.

questions.title: A few questions, then the picture
questions.body: Plainflow is building a picture of your idea. Each answer flips a switch on it. Some answers are already guessed from your sentence; change anything that's wrong.
questions.aside: There are no wrong answers. An honest yes means a closer look, not a no.

questions.title: Tick what's true
questions.body: A list like this stands in for a run of yes or no questions. The small print under each item says what it means. Not sure? Skip it and we keep our guess.

questions.title: The answer, forming
questions.body: This updates as you answer. Watch it change; that's the point. Nothing here is final until a person signs it.

canvas.title: Your idea, as a picture
canvas.body: Each box is one part of your idea: the people it's about, the data, the tool, what it's for, and the companies that handle the data. Wires show where data goes; the thick amber ones carry personal data. The dashed line is the edge of your organisation: anything to the right of it is outside.
canvas.aside: You can drag boxes about, and nothing you do here is final.

canvas.title: The sentence is the picture
canvas.body: Hover a word to light up where that data goes. Click one to open its box.

canvas.title: When it looks right
canvas.body: Have a look round first. Then press this and Plainflow reads the answer off the picture: can you do it, does policy allow it, and what to do next.

screening.title: The form your DPO signs
screening.body: Everything here came from your picture: the screening questions with the reason for each answer, the data's level, and what still needs a person. You don't need to read it; it's here so your DPO can.

rules.title: How the answers are worked out
rules.body: Every answer Plainflow gives comes from this table, not from hidden code. It's here so a DPO can check a rule and change it. You don't need to read it unless you want to see why something was said.

compare.title: Two versions side by side
compare.body: A is the copy you pinned; B is the picture as it is now. What changed is listed, and the to-do list shows what each version needs. Keep A, or go with B.

answer.title: The answer, read off the picture
answer.body: Everything on the right comes from the picture: whether you can do it, the facts behind that, and a list of things to do. From now on it's live: change the picture and the answer changes with it.
answer.aside: Nothing here is final until a person signs it.

answer.title: Flip any switch
answer.body: Switches are the choices you made in the questions. Flip one and the answer updates straight away, and a box on the right says what changed. Hover a switch to see what it means.

answer.title: Your answer
answer.body: Can you do it, in plain words, then the facts behind it: the data, policy, and whether a DPIA is needed. Click a fact to see why.

answer.title: What to do
answer.body: Each line is one thing that needs doing before this goes ahead, with who does it and roughly how long. Click a line to see what it is and why it's there.

answer.title: Tools
answer.body: Add a box and it arrives wired in, so the answer changes straight away. Undo takes anything back. Tidy the layout, fold boxes to their titles, or pin a copy to compare two versions.

answer.title: Save, and the record
answer.body: Save keeps the picture as a file you can open again. Record is the form your DPO signs, filled in from the picture.

report.title: What the code shows
report.body: This is everything the scan found in the code, with the exact lines as evidence, and what each finding does not prove. It's the raw material. The answer that counts is on the Canvas, where your answers fill in what code can't tell.
report.aside: Each card opens to show the code and the reasoning.
